title_ar: هل الذي ليس سلفي العقيدة مشرك؟
title_en: Is Someone Who Is Not Salafi in Creed an Associator of Partners with God?
body_ar: لا لأن المقصود هنا في الاعتقاد أن يكون الإنسان مؤمنا بالله وملائكته و كتبه و رسله و اليوم الآخر و القدر خيره و شره فمن كان مؤمنا بهذه فهو المسلم و من كان كافرا بأحد هذه فليس بمسلم فإذا هذا هو الفرق بين المسلم و الكافر هو هذه الأمور الستة و من لا يعلم من العقيدة إلا هذه الأمور الستة ناج يوم القيامة من لم يكن يعلم أي شيء إلا أنه يؤمن بالله و يؤمن بالملائكة و يؤمن بالكتب المنزلة و يؤمن بالرسل إجمالا لا تفصيلا و يؤمن كذلك باليوم الآخر إجمالا لا تفصيلا و يؤمن بالقدر خيره و شره هذا مؤمن قطعا لو مات على هذا دخل الجنة.
body_en: No. Because what is meant here in the matter of belief is that a person believe in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the divine decree (al-qadar), its good and its evil. Whoever believes in these is a Muslim, and whoever disbelieves in any one of them is not a Muslim. So this is the difference between the Muslim and the disbeliever: these six matters. And whoever knows nothing of creed (ʿaqīdah) beyond these six matters is saved on the Day of Resurrection. Someone who knew nothing whatever except that he believes in God, and believes in the angels, and believes in the revealed books, and believes in the messengers in a general way and not in detail, and likewise believes in the Last Day in a general way and not in detail, and believes in the divine decree, its good and its evil — this person is a believer beyond question. If he died upon this, he would enter the Garden.

flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW. The record is a ruling on who does and does not count as a Muslim, framed around a contemporary sectarian label. The Sheikh's answer is de-escalating — he reduces the criterion to the six articles of faith and explicitly says that someone who knows nothing beyond them is saved — but a text of this kind, extracted from its setting and read in English, is easily quoted in either direction. Translated faithfully, neither softened nor strengthened; the publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-21 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
The title is rendered with 'associator of partners with God' for mushrik rather than the bare transliteration, per the glossary entry for shirk.
'Salafi' is left as the source has it; it is the questioner's word, not the Sheikh's, and he does not define it or engage with the label in his answer.
The Sheikh answers only the question of who counts as a Muslim. He says nothing here about the correctness or otherwise of any school of creed, and nothing on that has been added.
